newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Maryborough says rain delays sugar.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Maryborough says rain delays sugar.

text.p: Queensland sugar grower and manufacturer Maryborough Sugar Factory Ltd said on Tuesday that good rains last week caused delays in the harvesting of sugar.

To the week ended September 28, Maryborough had crushed 418,867 tonnes of sugar cane at a commercial contained sugar (CCS) rate of 13.59 units, yielding 56,790 tonnes of 94 net titre (NT) raw sugar, Maryborough said.
This compares with 333,471 tonnes of cane crushed at a CCS of 13.47, producing 45,429 tonnes of 94 NT raws, a year earlier, it said.
A 1996 crop estimate of 675,000 tonnes will be a record if totally harvested, Maryborough said.
The 1996 crushing operations started on July 15. The harvest is expected to close in late November.
While the early October rains caused delays to this year's harvest, they will be of benefit to next year's crop, Maryborough said.
CCS measures the sugar content of the cane while 94 NT, a measure of the polarity of sugar crystals, is the standard used in Australia for sugar payments.
